purpose: A structured set of practical heuristics for agentic software development, emphasizing context control, workflow design, verification, and iterative refinement.

top_level_principle.name: Own the system, not just the prompt
top_level_principle.summary: Agent performance is shaped less by clever prompting alone and more by the design of the surrounding workflow: task boundaries, context quality, rules, verification, and cleanup.
implications: Do not rely on raw model intelligence alone.
Design the environment in which the agent works.
Assume responsibility for the outcome even when delegation is heavy.

heuristics.name: Prefer the thinnest viable workflow
heuristics.summary: Use the minimum tooling, abstraction, and orchestration necessary to solve the real problem you currently have.
why_it_matters: Every added layer increases cognitive overhead.
Many agent pain points are temporary and may disappear as base models and products improve.
Complex harnesses can lock teams into solutions for problems that later become irrelevant.
Simple workflows also make it easier to understand, revert, or isolate mistakes when agents act incorrectly.
signals_of_good_use: The workflow is easy to explain.
Each added tool solves a clearly observable problem.
Removing a tool would create a specific regression.
Changes are easy to isolate or revert if they prove incorrect.
failure_modes: debugging the harness instead of solving the task
agent_instruction_pattern: Use built-in capabilities first.
Only invoke specialized layers when they provide clear incremental value.
human_review_questions: What real problem does this tool solve?
Would we still choose this layer if the model improved next month?
Is the complexity proportional to the pain it removes?
when_it_breaks: Enterprise governance requirements
strict auditability needs
complex multi-repo orchestration
security or compliance environments requiring explicit control layers

heuristics.name: Treat context as a scarce resource
heuristics.summary: Provide the exact context needed for the current task and avoid flooding the agent with stale, global, or irrelevant information.
why_it_matters: Too much context reduces signal-to-noise ratio.
Irrelevant instructions can distort reasoning and implementation.
Agent failures often stem from confusion, not lack of capability.
signals_of_good_use: The agent is working from a small set of relevant files and instructions.
There is little evidence of the agent dragging unrelated history into the task.
The task prompt and working context are tightly aligned.
failure_modes: loading broad repo history into narrow implementation tasks
agent_instruction_pattern: Before acting, load only the task plan, the acceptance criteria, and the relevant files.
Do not consult unrelated memory or historical notes unless explicitly required.
human_review_questions: What information is essential for this task?
What information is merely available but not useful?
What prior instructions could conflict with this work?
when_it_breaks: Deep architectural investigations
cross-cutting migrations
tasks where local changes depend on broad system invariants

heuristics.name: Separate research from implementation
heuristics.summary: Do not force the same execution context to both explore solution options and implement one of them unless necessary.
why_it_matters: Research expands the option space.
Implementation benefits from narrowed constraints.
Mixing both modes encourages silent assumption-making and muddy execution.
signals_of_good_use: A design or decision phase exists before coding begins.
The implementation task references a chosen approach rather than an open-ended problem.
Agents are not simultaneously debating architecture and writing code.
failure_modes: hidden architecture decisions made during coding
agent_instruction_pattern: If implementation details are not fixed, first produce a bounded research memo comparing options.
After a decision is made, begin a fresh implementation task using only the chosen design.
human_review_questions: Has the implementation target actually been selected?
Is this coding task secretly still a design problem?
Would a fresh execution context improve focus?
when_it_breaks: Legacy systems where discovery and implementation must interleave
rapid prototyping
spike tasks intended to test feasibility rather than produce final code

heuristics.name: Use neutral prompts for investigation
heuristics.summary: When asking agents to inspect, debug, or review, avoid prompts that presuppose the conclusion.
why_it_matters: Agents are highly compliant and can be biased toward producing the requested kind of finding.
A prompt that assumes a bug exists often increases false positives.
Neutral phrasing improves the balance between discovery and skepticism.
signals_of_good_use: The prompt asks the agent to inspect and report findings rather than prove a specific outcome.
Outputs include confirmed findings, ambiguous findings, and no-issue findings when appropriate.
The agent distinguishes evidence from speculation.
agent_instruction_pattern: Trace the logic of the component and report all findings, separating confirmed issues, possible concerns, and normal behavior.
human_review_questions: Did I ask the agent to discover, or did I ask it to justify my suspicion?
Are the reported problems grounded in observable evidence?
What would a neutral reading of the same code say?
when_it_breaks: Targeted red-team tasks where forcing a threat-seeking posture is deliberate
time-boxed reviews focused on one known risk class

heuristics.name: Exploit adversarial analysis, but do not trust it blindly
heuristics.summary: Use multiple passes with different incentives or roles to improve reliability, but keep human or external verification in the loop.
why_it_matters: One agent may overproduce issues.
A second agent can challenge those claims.
A third pass can arbitrate, creating a more disciplined review pipeline.
signals_of_good_use: Generator and critic roles are clearly distinct.
Claims are evaluated against evidence, not just rhetoric.
The final output preserves uncertainty where appropriate.
failure_modes: false confidence from multiple agreeing agents
referee agents inheriting the same blind spots as the others
agent_instruction_pattern: Pass 1: enumerate possible issues broadly.
Pass 2: aggressively challenge each issue with evidence.
Pass 3: reconcile the two and classify each claim.
human_review_questions: Are these truly independent perspectives, or just the same model talking to itself three times?
What external evidence verifies the disputed findings?
Which claims remain uncertain even after arbitration?
when_it_breaks: When all passes share the same missing evidence
when the reviewer accepts arbitration output without inspection
when the task requires domain knowledge absent from all participants

heuristics.name: Assumptions are a primary failure source
heuristics.summary: Agent quality often collapses when missing information forces the model to infer intent, invariants, or system behavior without adequate grounding.
why_it_matters: Agents are much stronger at working from explicit constraints than at filling in invisible context.
Undocumented tribal knowledge creates hidden traps.
Unstated assumptions turn plausible output into unreliable output.
Persisting decisions, plans, and assumptions in lightweight artifacts (task plans, notes, or logs) reduces reliance on transient conversational context.
signals_of_good_use: The task includes explicit constraints and definitions.
Unknowns are surfaced instead of silently guessed.
The agent re-reads task plans and relevant files before continuing after interruption.
Important assumptions and decisions are written into task artifacts rather than remaining implicit in conversation history.
agent_instruction_pattern: If required information is missing, state the gap explicitly.
Re-read the task plan and the relevant files before resuming after context loss or compaction.
When assumptions, plans, or unresolved questions become significant to the task, record them in a durable artifact rather than relying on session memory.
If uncertainty prevents confident execution, pause and surface the uncertainty rather than proceeding with guessed requirements.
human_review_questions: What is the agent assuming here?
Which invariant exists in my head but not in the repo or task spec?
Did the failure expose a documentation gap rather than only a model gap?
when_it_breaks: Exploratory ideation tasks
brainstorming sessions where assumptions are part of the exercise

heuristics.name: Define termination explicitly
heuristics.summary: Agents need concrete, testable definitions of done because they do not reliably infer when a task is truly complete.
why_it_matters: Without a finish line, agents often stop at a plausible midpoint.
Stubs, partial implementations, and unverified completions become common.
Deterministic completion criteria improve both execution quality and trust.
Tasks that are too large often lack clear termination conditions and verification scope.
signals_of_good_use: The task has explicit acceptance criteria.
Tests or checks define minimum completion conditions.
The agent is not allowed to declare success without verification.
failure_modes: passing descriptions of work instead of completed work
agent_instruction_pattern: The task is not complete until all specified checks pass.
Do not modify the acceptance tests unless explicitly instructed to revise the contract itself.
human_review_questions: How would I know this task is complete if a human handed it back to me?
What objective checks prove the work is done?
What loopholes allow false completion?
Is the task small enough that its completion criteria are unambiguous?
when_it_breaks: Open-ended research
creative ideation
prototype spikes where learning is the goal rather than production readiness

heuristics.name: Use layered verification
heuristics.summary: Combine multiple forms of verification such as tests, screenshots, logs, and behavioral checks rather than relying on one signal alone.
why_it_matters: Passing tests do not guarantee correct user experience.
Visual checks catch classes of problems not covered by logic tests.
Layered verification reduces blind spots.
Different classes of evidence (static checks, runtime behavior, visual inspection, and requirement alignment) catch different failure modes.
signals_of_good_use: Functional checks exist for behavior.
Visual or observational checks exist for UI-sensitive work.
Verification is aligned with the actual risk profile of the task.
Verification uses multiple evidence types when risk justifies it (for example: tests + logs + UI confirmation).
failure_modes: false security from one green signal
agent_instruction_pattern: Run the functional checks first.
Then run or inspect visual or behavioral verification appropriate to the task.
Report mismatches rather than declaring victory on partial evidence.
human_review_questions: What kind of failure would this verification miss?
Is this UI behavior correct, or merely test-passing?
Do we need semantic, visual, and integration-level evidence?
What class of evidence is missing from this verification?
when_it_breaks: Extremely small internal changes where broader verification is wasteful
non-UI utilities with narrowly bounded behavior

heuristics.name: Prefer fresh sessions for bounded work
heuristics.summary: Use a new session or execution context per contract-sized unit of work whenever practical.
why_it_matters: Fresh sessions reduce contamination from prior tasks.
Bounded work units are easier to reason about, reproduce, and verify.
Long-running sessions often accumulate unrelated context and drift.
signals_of_good_use: Each unit of work has a clear contract or task spec.
The agent is not carrying large amounts of history across unrelated tasks.
Failures can be isolated to one task context.
agent_instruction_pattern: Treat each contract as a separate execution unit unless continuity is essential.
Load only the contract, the relevant files, and the required rules.
human_review_questions: Would a fresh start improve clarity here?
What useful state would actually be lost by restarting?
Is this session carrying too many unrelated goals?
when_it_breaks: deep exploratory refactors
multi-stage investigations with heavy accumulated evidence
interactive debugging where continuity is the main asset

heuristics.name: Encode preferences as rules and recipes as skills
heuristics.summary: Distinguish between constraints on behavior and reusable procedures for solving recurring classes of tasks.
why_it_matters: Not all repeated guidance is the same.
Rules prevent unwanted behavior.
Skills operationalize preferred methods.
signals_of_good_use: Rules are concise and normative.
Skills are procedural and scenario-specific.
The routing layer only loads what is relevant.
failure_modes: mixing prohibitions and procedures into giant instruction files
loading every rule and skill for every task
agent_instruction_pattern: Read rules before acting in the governed domain.
Invoke the relevant skill when the scenario matches the skill's intended use.
human_review_questions: Is this guidance a constraint or a recipe?
Would a future agent know when this applies?
Can this be named and routed more clearly?
when_it_breaks: Very small solo projects where explicit operational memory is unnecessary
highly novel work with little repeatability

heuristics.name: Use the root instruction file as a router, not a landfill
heuristics.summary: A top-level agent instruction file should primarily direct the agent to the right context, rather than contain every rule, skill, and preference inline.
why_it_matters: Routing preserves focus.
A compact entrypoint reduces startup confusion.
Conditional loading is more scalable than global loading.
signals_of_good_use: The root file is short and organized.
It contains branching logic or routing guidance.
Detailed instructions live in smaller specialized files.
failure_modes: startup overload from reading everything every time
agent_instruction_pattern: Start from the root router.
Load only the branch relevant to the current task type and state.
human_review_questions: Does this file direct, or does it dump?
Can a new contributor understand the routing logic quickly?
What instructions belong in specialized leaves instead of the root?
when_it_breaks: Tiny projects with only one work mode
tasks so simple that routing overhead exceeds the benefit

heuristics.name: Continuously prune and consolidate
heuristics.summary: Rules, skills, and orchestration logic naturally decay; periodically refactor them to remove contradictions, duplication, and stale guidance.
why_it_matters: Append-only process memory becomes noisy and self-conflicting.
Old instructions can outlive the conditions that made them useful.
Performance often declines gradually as operational memory grows.
signals_of_good_use: Periodic reviews of rules and skills occur.
Redundant instructions are merged.
Outdated guidance is archived or deleted.
failure_modes: workflow regression caused by stale process memory
agent_instruction_pattern: Periodically review operational guidance for duplication, contradictions, and stale assumptions.
Propose consolidation where multiple files appear to govern the same scenario.
human_review_questions: What instructions no longer reflect current practice?
Which files overlap?
Have we been adding guidance faster than we refine it?
when_it_breaks: Emergency situations where speed matters more than elegance
new systems still too early in their lifecycle to consolidate meaningfully

heuristics.name: Iterate from observed failure, not imagined perfection
heuristics.summary: Start with a simple workflow, watch where it fails in practice, and add structure only where evidence justifies it.
why_it_matters: Early overdesign creates friction without proven value.
Observed failure modes produce better rules than speculative fears.
This mirrors how strong engineering systems evolve over time.
signals_of_good_use: Each added rule or skill is traceable to a real recurring issue.
The workflow remains understandable as it grows.
Teams can explain why a given structure exists.
failure_modes: operational bureaucracy detached from real problems
agent_instruction_pattern: When failure recurs, capture the pattern and propose a targeted rule or skill.
Do not generalize one-off anomalies into global process unless repetition justifies it.
human_review_questions: What real failure led to this structure?
Is this rule solving a recurring problem or a single anecdote?
Would a simpler mechanism achieve the same protection?
when_it_breaks: high-risk domains where speculative safeguards are warranted before incidents occur

heuristics.name: Product convergence is a clue, not a law
heuristics.summary: When multiple frontier tools adopt a feature, that is evidence of usefulness, but not proof that the feature is universally optimal or sufficient.
why_it_matters: Convergence often indicates repeated real-world demand.
Built-in support lowers maintenance burden for users.
But vendor productization is shaped by market and product concerns, not only truth.
signals_of_good_use: A feature is supported by multiple major platforms.
The feature solves a recurring operational problem directly.
Built-in support meaningfully reduces custom scaffolding.
failure_modes: assuming official support means universal best practice
ignoring valuable niche tools because they are not mainstream
agent_instruction_pattern: Prefer built-in solutions for broadly common needs, but remain open to specialized tools when the problem warrants them.
human_review_questions: Is this feature popular because it is useful, or merely because it is visible?
Do our constraints match the mainstream use case?
Would a niche solution still be better for this context?
when_it_breaks: specialized enterprise needs
novel workflows not yet represented in mainstream products
edge cases outside vendor priority

heuristics.name: Always preserve human accountability
heuristics.summary: Delegation does not remove responsibility; the human operator or team remains accountable for correctness, risk, and downstream impact.
why_it_matters: Agents can accelerate design and implementation but still produce subtle errors.
Confidence generated by speed or fluency can mask risk.
Real software systems carry user, business, and operational consequences.
signals_of_good_use: A human validates high-risk outputs.
Critical paths receive explicit review and verification.
The team understands that delegation changes labor, not ownership.
failure_modes: trusting fluent output as proof of correctness
diffusing responsibility because 'the agent did it'
agent_instruction_pattern: Provide evidence for claims and implementation choices.
Surface uncertainty clearly so a human reviewer can make the final judgment where needed.
human_review_questions: What would I still be responsible for if this failed in production?
Which parts of this output deserve the highest scrutiny?
Am I reviewing substance, or just admiring fluency?
when_it_breaks: It does not truly break; it is a governing principle across all other heuristics.

recommended_operating_sequence: Decide whether this is research, implementation, investigation, or verification.
Route to the necessary rules and skills.
Execute in a fresh session when practical.
Capture recurring lessons as rules or skills.

anti_patterns.name: Prompt-and-pray
anti_patterns.description: Giving a vague high-level request and assuming model intelligence will compensate for missing design, context, and acceptance criteria.

anti_patterns.name: Instruction landfill
anti_patterns.description: Stuffing every rule, preference, and memory into one giant root file.

anti_patterns.name: Context maximalism
anti_patterns.description: Assuming more context is always better, regardless of relevance.

anti_patterns.name: Single-signal trust
anti_patterns.description: Treating one passing test, one screenshot, or one agent opinion as sufficient proof.

anti_patterns.name: Session immortality
anti_patterns.description: Keeping agents running indefinitely across unrelated tasks and expecting stable performance.

anti_patterns.name: Vendor determinism
anti_patterns.description: Assuming official product features are always the best answer for every workflow.

anti_patterns.name: Ephemeral reasoning
anti_patterns.description: Allowing critical decisions, assumptions, or plans to exist only in transient session context rather than recording them in inspectable artifacts.

compact_agent_facing_summary.mission: Operate with bounded context, explicit goals, and verifiable completion.
rules_of_thumb: Load less, but make it relevant.
Do research and implementation in separate phases when possible.
Do not infer missing requirements silently.
Use neutral investigation language unless adversarial posture is explicitly requested.
Do not declare completion without passing the stated checks.
Prefer fresh task contexts for bounded units of work.
Use rules for constraints and skills for repeatable methods.
Treat root instructions as routing logic.
Surface uncertainty and preserve human accountability.
